title: Joe Brady Gives An Injury Update For Monday's Game Against The Vikings
headline: Josh Palmer is the only Bills player ruled out for Monday night at Minnesota. Dion Dawkins is questionable after missing practice but is expected to be given every chance to play.
summary: Joe Brady opened with the injury report: Josh Palmer is out, and Dion Dawkins, Jordan Hancock and two or three others (heard as Alex Anderson, Greg Gaines and Tyrell Shavers) are questionable. He said IR is not under consideration for Palmer right now. He explained that Dawkins sat out practice as a veteran rest plan, and that experienced players at certain positions can be ready without a full week of reps. He compared Dawkins to Christian Benford before the Rams game, to DJ Moore, and to Spencer Brown last week. Brady said the line prepares for backups and position shuffles during the week, so a changed combination wouldn't force him to alter the play calling. He praised the line coaching and depth development, singling out the young tackle (heard as 'Graves', most likely Tylan Grable), who has moved from right tackle last week to prepping at left tackle. He said the Vikings' defense, which he called the best in the NFL at scoring, often plays base personnel against 11 personnel, which is a growing league trend. He said the running backs will face an above-average pass-protection test this week and need to clean up technique after a low-blocking penalty last week. He closed by saying the team's standard shouldn't change with the opponent and that players should avoid trying to be heroes.

Did not practice this week as a planned veteran rest. Brady trusts him to be ready and will keep evaluating through Monday.
Listed as questionable for Monday with no further detail.

signals.claim: Palmer will miss Monday night's game against the Vikings.
signals.note: With Palmer out, the Bills' other receivers pick up his targets and snaps in a tough matchup.
signals.quote: Joshua Palmer the only one that is out.

signals.claim: Dawkins is expected to be given every chance to play Monday despite no practice reps this week, pending further evaluation.
signals.note: His status affects the left side of the line, which matters for Josh Allen and the run game against a tough defense.

signals.claim: Grable can move from right tackle to left tackle this week if needed, with no drop-off in the offense.
signals.note: If Dawkins can't go, Grable is the likely fill-in at left tackle, and Brady said he wouldn't change his play calling.
signals.quote: I don't think he would blink.

topics.detail: Besides Dawkins and Hancock, players heard as Alex Anderson, Greg Gaines and Tyrell Shavers were also listed as questionable. These names are not on the supplied roster, so they were not confirmed.

Brady credited the line coaches for developing backups who step in without a drop-off. He said the starting five don't take every practice rep, so the team prepares for different combinations and different players snapping to Josh Allen.

Brady called it good but said it faces an unusually big test this week. The backs need to clean up technique after a low-blocking penalty last week, and he said pass pro matters to them as much as running the ball.
Minnesota often plays base personnel against 11 personnel, trusting its players to match up in space. Brady sees this as a growing league trend that takes a coach and players who trust the scheme.
Brady said the team's standard shouldn't rise or fall with the opponent. He wants players to avoid being heroes and just play the next play, which is what he means by 'competitive stamina'.

title: Kevin O’Connell on Aaron Jones Being Nominated for Salute to Service Award & Preparing for Vikings vs. Bills Monday Night
headline: Kyler Murray, Jauan Jennings and Demond Claiborne are all out Monday night vs. the Bills, so Carson Wentz starts and Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison are the healthy top receivers.
summary: O'Connell opened by praising Aaron Jones as the Vikings' Salute to Service nominee. He then gave injury news. Demond Claiborne (knee) and Jauan Jennings (calf strain) were hurt at Thursday practice, and both are out Monday along with Kyler Murray. Theo Jackson (quad) and Jay Ward (knee) are questionable, and nobody else carries a designation. Murray spent the week in treatment, and the plan is to see how he moves Monday and then how he feels heading into a short week. Without Jennings, Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison are healthy, and the staff is deciding between an elevation from the practice squad and a mix of other receivers, working backward from red zone, third down and early downs. With Carson Wentz in, O'Connell said Minnesota has been in shotgun a lot on early downs. He praised Wentz's RPO experience and size, and said they could be under center more depending on what the defense shows. He called the Bills' defensive front very talented and an aggressive blitzing group. He stressed quick, rhythm-based passing and total-team pass protection. The rest of the session covered a conversation with a player named Jordan about a possible roster move that didn't happen, and memories of coaching Adrian Peterson.

topics.detail: O'Connell called the Bills' defensive front really talented and said it blitzes aggressively. Minnesota needs to get its playmakers activated on early downs. He emphasized a rhythm-based offense with the ball out on time so pass protection can be aggressive.
The offense has been in shotgun more than previously, especially on early downs, to pair the run and pass. With Wentz it can use more under-center looks and RPOs, depending on what the defense shows.
Jones is the team's Salute to Service nominee, and fans can vote online. O'Connell praised his work with current and former service members.

Asked about a past conversation with a player named Jordan regarding a possible roster move that didn't happen, O'Connell said both sides handled it well. He said the player loves being a Minnesota Viking.
O'Connell reminisced about working out Peterson in Washington and called him an absolute machine. He also praised East Texas as a talent hotbed. Nothing fantasy-relevant.
